name: Taiwan High Speed Rail N700ST
description: Taiwan High Speed Rail and the Hitachi Toshiba Supreme Consortium adapted the N700S design for Taiwan. The 12-car model was tailored to the operator’s environment and passenger service needs.

places.note: The first complete trainset was shipped from Japan. Main-line validation took place in Taiwan.

date.label: 20 August 2025
date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: Taiwan High Speed Rail disclosed the N700ST designation and described its localized design while the first trainset was being manufactured.

evidence.supports: The dated notice names the type, describes design changes and reports manufacture underway.

date.label: 30 July 2026
date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: The Hitachi Toshiba Supreme Consortium reported completing and shipping the first 12-car N700ST trainset from Japan.
events.caveats: The announcement supplies a date by which the first trainset had shipped.

evidence.locator: Opening two paragraphs and Overview of Railcars
evidence.supports: The manufacturer reports completion and shipment of the first trainset on its 30 July announcement.

date.label: 15 August 2026
date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: The first complete N700ST trainset arrived in Taiwan from Japan.

evidence.supports: The test report gives the earlier arrival date.
The manufacturer identifies the trainset that was shipped to Taiwan.

date.label: 16 November 2026
date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: The first N700ST trainset reached 170 km/h in its first main-line trial, between Yanchao and Chiayi.
events.caveats: The milestone was a test of the train and its interaction with the track and overhead power. Passenger service was planned from 1 July 2027.

evidence.supports: The operator gives the date, section, measured trial speed and integration aim.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated milestone retained here for this design or deployment.

links.statement: The Hitachi Toshiba Supreme Consortium based Taiwan’s N700ST on JR Central’s N700S model and tailored it to THSRC’s operating and service requirements.

evidence.locator: Opening two paragraphs and Overview of Railcars
evidence.supports: The manufacturer identifies the source design and attributes the localization to THSRC requirements.
The receiving operator independently identifies the design basis and documents interior, exterior and functional adaptation.
